summary.name: Tamka
summary.one_liner: Tamka is a free, open-source macOS dictation app that runs NVIDIA Parakeet speech models offline on the Neural Engine and types the recognised text at your cursor.
use_cases: dictate emails and chat messages on a Mac
type text into a code editor by voice
transcribe meetings and recordings from a microphone
summary.what_it_does: Tamka starts and stops dictation with a keyboard shortcut (Control-V by default) and types the recognised text at the cursor in any app, also keeping a copy on the clipboard. Speech recognition runs on the Neural Engine using NVIDIA Parakeet models, and audio stays on the Mac. Before typing it removes filler words like "um" and "uh", collapses stutters, and converts spoken commands such as "comma", "new line" or "open paren" into symbols; the page lists 112 default commands. It offers several models (Parakeet Ultra, Phonon-2, v3, v2, and Apple Speech), a menu bar icon, a microphone picker, and a "Transcribe Last Recording Again" option. The page reports Parakeet Ultra made 7.7% word errors against 9.9% for Whisper large-v3-turbo on 117 recordings, using about 0.5 GB of memory.
notable: Runs NVIDIA Parakeet models offline on the Apple Neural Engine; audio never leaves the Mac
Spoken commands and cleanup: filler removal, stutter collapsing, and 112 default voice-to-symbol commands
Open source under GNU GPL v3.0 or later; signed and notarized release zip
Reported word error rate 7.7% vs 9.9% for Whisper large-v3-turbo on the author's benchmark
caveats: Requires Apple silicon Mac on macOS 26 or later
Needs a speech model download first (Parakeet Ultra is 632 MB); the app does not include a model
Benchmark is by the author; the difference without meeting recordings is within the margin of error
Without Accessibility permission it copies text but cannot paste it
